summary.intent: Investigate the someguy IPFS sidecar state on staging, diagnose performance issues, upgrade Kubo, and get the stack into a stable baseline for post-phase-19 performance testing.
summary.outcome: Diagnosed someguy's IPNS endpoint as completely non-functional (hanging indefinitely on PUT/GET while /providers/ works fine); upgraded Kubo from v0.34.0 to v0.40.0 with full E2E and load test validation; removed someguy from staging and reverted to delegated-ipfs.dev; fixed Grafana provisioning 503s with a readiness poll; filed a todo to investigate someguy locally.

repo: Someguy's /routing/v1/providers/ endpoint works fine but /routing/v1/ipns/ hangs indefinitely — IPNS PUT/GET never return a response even with 30s timeout
The docker/ directory (docker-compose.yml, Caddyfile, alloy-config.river) is committed to the repo but generated/SCP'd to the VPS during CI — not gitignored but also not deployed via git pull
DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL defaults to https://delegated-ipfs.dev in delegated-routing.client.ts:24 but is overridden by .env.staging on the server
IPNS delegated routing publish is fire-and-forget since PR #308 — failures are warnings, not errors, so the API returns 200 even when someguy times out
Release-please only triggers releases for feat and fix commit types by default — build, perf, revert do not generate releases without explicit changelog-sections config
Grafana Cloud free-tier instance sleeps when idle and returns 503 'Your instance is loading' — provisioning must wait for /api/health to return 200 before pushing dashboards
The alloy-config.river scrapes someguy metrics and needed to be updated alongside the compose file when removing the service

code.finding: Default fallback URL is https://delegated-ipfs.dev — used when DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL env var is not set
Rate limiting can be bypassed with X-Throttle-Bypass header using THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET — E2E tests require this header, not NODE_ENV=test

workflow: Running all vitest load test scenarios concurrently causes interference — sustained-load's 5-min duration overlaps with other tests and can cause Cloudflare 522s from connection exhaustion
NODE_ENV in .env file overrides shell environment — changing NODE_ENV=test in shell doesn't affect NestJS ConfigModule which reads .env directly
ThrottlerModule has hardcoded limits (10 req/s, 100 req/min) with no NODE_ENV=test relaxation — load/E2E tests must use the bypass header
git amend + force push is appropriate for fixing commit message type before merge when a release hasn't been cut yet
Kubo v0.40.0 breaking changes are all gateway-related (IPIP-524, IPIP-523); RPC API (/api/v0/*) is unaffected

friction: Someguy 'disable' from a prior session was never persisted — it either wasn't committed or was overwritten by a subsequent deploy that reset .env.staging from the workflow defaults
Load test harness marks operations as errors silently — high error rates (95%+) passed all test assertions because the harness treats SDK exceptions as metric data points, not test failures
The build commit type doesn't trigger Release Please by default — required a config change before the Kubo upgrade would produce a release
THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET was not documented in the SDK E2E test README or .env.example — caused repeated 429 failures before the bypass mechanism was discovered
CodeRabbit's description of Kubo v0.40.1 as 'stability improvements' was misleading — it's a Windows-only Go toolchain downgrade
open_items: Investigate someguy IPNS failure locally: add someguy v0.11.1 to docker-compose.yml, point DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL at it, reproduce the /routing/v1/ipns/ hang, and check someguy GitHub issues for known IPNS bugs
Run post-phase-19 performance baselines against staging once the Kubo v0.40.0 + delegated-ipfs.dev changes are deployed — compare against phase 18 p50/p95/p99 metrics
PR #322 (release-please config + someguy removal + Kubo staging deploy) needs review and merge to trigger a release
